actuator_details: Two 7-DoF arms (Robotis Dynamixel servos), spherical wrist, anthropomorphic 5-finger hand options, 3-DoF Orbita-prototype neck. 3D-printed structural elements published under open hardware licenses. CAD released as STL/STEP; firmware on Dynamixel U2D2/USB2AX bus.
control_architecture: ROS1/ROS2 stack with reachy-sdk Python API, IK solver via PyKDL/Pinocchio. Designed explicitly as research substrate; firmware and SDK open-sourced on GitHub (pollen-robotics/reachy).
creator: Pollen Robotics / INRIA Flowers (Pierre Rouanet, Matthieu Lapeyre, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer)
disclosure_citation: Mick, Sébastien, Lapeyre, Matthieu, Rouanet, Pierre, Halgand, Christophe, Benois-Pineau, Jenny, Paclet, Florent, Cattaert, Daniel, Oudeyer, Pierre-Yves, de Rugy, Aymar. 'Reachy, a 3D-Printed Human-Like Robotic Arm as a Testbed for Human-Robot Control Strategies.' Frontiers in Neurorobotics 13:65, September 2019. Original release: Pollen Robotics / INRIA Flowers, 2017 GitHub release of Reachy v1 (poppy-project lineage).
prior_art_notes: Reachy 1 (Pollen Robotics 2017, INRIA Flowers lineage) is one of the earliest fully-open-hardware humanoid torso platforms with a published research-grade SDK predating commercial offerings. Anticipates with full specificity: (1) claims on 3D-printed open-hardware humanoid arms with Dynamixel-class actuation — Reachy 1's STL/STEP CAD and firmware are publicly archived since 2017; (2) claims on research-substrate Python SDKs for humanoid telemanipulation — reachy-sdk on GitHub at v0.x predates most commercial humanoid SDK offerings; (3) claims on dual-arm research-platform configurations with anthropomorphic spherical wrists. The 2019 Frontiers paper provides peer-reviewed timestamped disclosure; GitHub commits provide finer-grained 2016-2017 priority. Existing corpus 'reachy' entry should reference this v1 ancestor. Modern open-humanoid IP filings face Reachy 1 at 9-year-deep anchor.
sensing: stereo cameras in head, head IMU, joint encoders
sources: Mick, S. et al. 'Reachy, a 3D-Printed Human-Like Robotic Arm.' Frontiers in Neurorobotics 13:65, 2019.
Lapeyre, M. PhD Thesis (Poppy lineage). INRIA Flowers, 2014.
